status_summary: As of October 2026 race-conscious admissions and grant programs are an active Civil Rights Division enforcement area. Executive Order 14173 (2025-01-21) directed the Attorney General to produce a strategic enforcement plan, including up to nine potential compliance investigations per agency, and the Attorney General's memorandum of 2025-02-05 directed the Division to investigate and penalize unlawful DEI preferences in the private sector and at federally funded schools. On 2025-03-27 the Attorney General directed compliance reviews of admissions at Stanford, UC Berkeley, UCLA and UC Irvine. On 2026-02-06 the Fourth Circuit vacated the nationwide preliminary injunction against the order's certification provision, so the order is being enforced while as-applied challenges remain possible. The Division sought to intervene in a Students for Fair Admissions suit against UCLA's medical school (2026-01-28), issued Title VI and Students for Fair Admissions findings of race discrimination in admissions at UC Davis School of Medicine (2026-06-10), UCSF School of Medicine (2026-09-22) and UCLA School of Law (2026-10-01), saying in each case it will negotiate a settlement and sue if talks fail, and closed a Title VI review of a Minnesota grant program on 2026-07-07 after the state ended it. The public actions found are civil findings, compliance reviews and one intervention against public institutions; no suits or prosecutions by the Division against corporations or private employers were found in the sources reviewed, and the contents of the EO 14173 enforcement plan were not found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14173 signed (Federal Register 2025-01-31): revokes Executive Order 11246 and related orders, requires contractors and grantees to certify they run no unlawful DEI programs, and directs the Attorney General to submit an enforcement plan within 120 days.

The Attorney General's memorandum Ending Illegal DEI and DEIA Discrimination and Preferences directed the Civil Rights Division to investigate and penalize unlawful DEI preferences in the private sector and in federally funded schools, and called for a Division and Office of Legal Policy report by 2025-03-01 proposing a deterrence plan that could include criminal investigations and up to nine civil compliance investigations.
The Attorney General directed the Civil Rights Division to open compliance reviews of admissions policies at Stanford, UC Berkeley, UCLA and UC Irvine.

Harmeet Dhillon takes office as Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights after Senate confirmation on 2025-04-03 (52-45) and issues new mission statements for the Division's sections, per a secondary summary; the same summary reports early probes of DEI or affirmative action policies at Minnesota's Department of Human Services, George Mason University, and the University of California system and large attorney departures from the Division.
The Civil Rights Division seeks to intervene in a Central District of California lawsuit against UCLA's David Geffen School of Medicine over alleged race-conscious admissions.
The Fourth Circuit vacates the nationwide preliminary injunction against the certification and termination provisions of Executive Orders 14173 and 14151 and remands to the District of Maryland.
DOJ announces a finding that UC Davis School of Medicine discriminates based on race in admissions, citing Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard, and says it will negotiate a settlement or sue.

An interagency agreement gives the Civil Rights Division authority over certain school discrimination complaints that the Education Department would typically handle (as reported by Bloomberg Law on 2026-06-19).
DOJ announces it closed a Title VI compliance review of the Minnesota Department of Health's Capacity Strengthening Initiative after Minnesota repealed the enabling statute.

DOJ announced a finding that UCSF School of Medicine discriminated based on race in admissions for the 2023 to 2025 classes under Title VI and Students for Fair Admissions, and said it would negotiate a settlement or sue.

DOJ announces a finding that UCLA School of Law discriminated against white and Asian applicants in admissions for the 2023 to 2025 classes in violation of Title VI, and says it will continue investigating law schools.

title: Refocus Civil Rights Division on enforcement against DEI and race-conscious practices
uncertainties: The EO 14173 enforcement plan, the 2025-07 DOJ guidance to funding recipients, the Civil Rights Fraud Initiative and any private-employer cases were not found or searched in detail. The Attorney General memorandum of 2025-02-05 was read on justice.gov: it set a 2025-03-01 deadline for a Division and Office of Legal Policy report to the Associate Attorney General, and that report was not found; the memo lists criminal investigations only as possible proposals for the report. DOJ's 2026-06-10 release says UCLA's medical school and Yale's medical school received similar determinations the previous month; those releases were not opened. Dhillon-era staffing and early probe details come from a Wikipedia summary and a Bloomberg Law article; treat as leads. The Fourth Circuit ruling is reported by law-firm and compliance blogs, not the opinion. Whether the Mandate's first-year prosecution push has occurred in the form it describes (prosecutions versus civil Title VI findings) is a judgment not settled here.
